injections.why: R1274, the other direction and the one that reads as reassuring while being wrong: a run that used 95% of its budget is a MEASUREMENT — what it took is what it took — and calling it censored tells a reader that a number they can act on is a number nobody knows. `share_of` floors, so a hundred is the exact boundary rather than a round number somebody chose: 99.6% of a budget answers 99

injections.name: a-job-with-no-curve-at-all-is-left-out-of-the-block
injections.why: `movements` produces nothing for a job that has never completed, which is right — there is no cost curve — and would therefore take it silently out of a block that reads as covering every job in the record. Where the level line has just named that job, `no trend` is itself the news

injections.name: how-a-job-ended-is-thrown-away-with-what-it-took
injections.why: the level line wants every job that ran — the one its budget ended is the one it most needs to name — and a trend wants only the comparable ones. The record serves both, so it keeps GitHub's own word rather than a flag one of the two readers decided on

injections.name: a-record-shape-that-changed-prints-one-line-per-file
injections.why: the shape of a record is a type, so the day it changes EVERY record in the directory stops reading at once — thirty-two of them when R1261 added the conclusion, measured on this machine. One unreadable record is a fact worth a line; thirty are one fact, and a hundred lines of the same sentence is a block a reader learns to skip

injections.name: how-far-a-job-swings-on-its-own-is-not-printed
injections.why: R1270. Without it a reader has the ends and the range and no way to tell a movement from this job's noise — which is measured rather than supposed: R1268's ledger read `validate` gaining eleven points between two pushes as a budget running away, and that job moves by as much as thirteen between adjacent commits while nothing about it changes

injections.name: the-jitter-is-printed-for-a-window-of-two-runs
injections.why: R1270. With two completed runs there is ONE adjacent pair, so the largest move between adjacent commits IS the movement between the ends — printing it there is the same number twice, the second time wearing the word `own`, which tells a reader that the only measurement in the window is noise

injections.name: a-series-that-separates-in-one-place-is-read-as-a-climb
injections.why: R1270. A movement between the ends of a window reads as a slope, and a reader who reads it that way extrapolates a line nothing is on. `validate` is two levels with a jump between them and R1268's ledger recorded it as a climb

injections.name: one-clean-cut-is-enough-to-call-a-series-a-step
injections.why: R1270, and this is the clause that keeps the detector from firing on the steadiest climb in the repository. A series that rises every commit separates cleanly WHEREVER it is cut, so a rule that stopped at the first clean cut would send its reader to one arbitrary commit to look for a cause spread across all of them

injections.name: a-side-of-one-run-is-read-as-a-level
injections.why: R1270. `every run before is cheaper than every run after` is trivially true of any series whose first measurement happened to be its lowest, and this record's jobs move by eight to thirteen points between adjacent commits — so a one-run side is a claim about noise wearing the clothes of a claim about a level. IT REDDENS EIGHTEEN CASES AND THEY ARE ALL THE SAME HARM: a window of TWO runs becomes able to step at all, which is why the records built from two commits break, and a seven-run series gains a second separation at its first run, which is why the step case breaks with it. R1275 is why so many of them now say so out loud — a series that can step is a series this reporter goes to GitHub about, and every case whose record ought to hold no step reports through an `Unasked` source that PANICS when it is asked. The eleven extra reds are that fixture naming the cost this constant was silently buying

injections.name: where-a-cost-rose-is-looked-for-among-the-completed-runs
injections.why: R1275, and this is the defect N198 was open about. The LEVEL either side of a step is a cost, so it is drawn over runs that completed; WHERE the cost rose is a duration, and a change that makes a job dearer is often the change that breaks it — so the runs a rise lands on are disproportionately the ones a cost curve cannot hold. On this repository's own record the two populations answer two commits apart: the split is `4eccb3d4`, whose diff is a path-normalisation in one gate, and the level had been there since `a3005567` two runs earlier

injections.name: the-walk-back-to-the-rise-is-not-contiguous
injections.why: R1275, and this is what keeps the rise from being a lie. A job that hung once in its cheap era has one old row at 100% of its budget, and `the earliest run at or above the expensive level` names that row — sending a reader to a commit weeks before anything changed, under a sentence claiming the level has held ever since. What is asserted is narrower and is the thing a reader acts on: no run has been BELOW the level since

injections.why: R1275. The other end of the comparison has to be the last run at the CHEAP level; taking the row before the split instead lands inside the expensive band, and on this repository's record it lands on the rise itself — so the attribution compares a run against itself and reports that nothing inside the job moved, in the sentence whose whole purpose is to say what did

injections.name: a-skipped-step-is-read-as-a-step-that-took-no-time
injections.why: R1275, and the injection is this block's own first output rather than an imagined defect. GitHub does not send a skipped step with null stamps: it sends the START AND END OF THE STOPPAGE, equal to each other, so a duration read off the stamps is a well-formed `0 s`. Five steps of the cancelled run beside this repository's rise read that way, and the reporter said `mnemosyne-cli validate-workspace` had got ninety-six seconds CHEAPER on the run where it did not run at all — a fall, in the direction that offsets the rise being attributed

injections.name: the-bound-on-the-steps-that-did-not-rise-is-printed-with-a-sign
injections.why: R1275, and this too was the block's own first output. The clause exists to say that nothing ELSE in the job rose, and it printed the largest move among the rest — an absolute value — through the formatter that carries a sign. `moved by at most +1m36s` was a step that had got ninety-six seconds cheaper, and a reader adding the numbers up concludes the growth is spread across the job rather than sitting in one step

injections.name: a-step-is-identified-by-where-it-sits-in-the-list
injections.why: R1275. A step is identified by its NAME, and R1229 is why: it inserted a step into `validate`, so every step after it carries a different number in the later run than in the earlier one. Any comparison that lets position into the identity holds each step against its neighbour — a page of findings, none of them true, on the one commit where a reader most needs the answer
